tasks.short: Arrange a regular pickup for a customer or group.

steps.what: Read the pickup card for these particular customers or groups on this shuttle.
Arrange the pickup on the regular schedule with that customer or group.

tasks.design: A pickup card in the cab lists the customer or group, the place, the usual time, and the days. The dispatcher writes it when the standing booking is set. The driver reads it, then still arranges the pickup with that customer or group. If the card has no row, the driver uses the paper booking in the same step.
tasks.previous_blocker: The standing days lived in the dispatcher's head or in an office folder the driver did not have in the cab.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper card with those four fields is enough. No new model is required.
tasks.still_hard: The customer can change the time on the day. The driver still has to agree it.
tasks.human_edge: The driver knows which passenger needs a slower pickup and which group waits together.
tasks.altitude: The driver still arranges the pickup. The card only shortens finding the standing days.

reach.learn: Read a standing stop card, then still agree the pickup with the household.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the customer or group, place, usual time, and days shortens the search when the row is there. The driver still arranges the pickup. Model knowledge.

Telematics and a driver app that observe location or behaviour need works-council consent under the cited article. This pickup task adds no telematics and no driver app. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited statute.

Scoring drivers or allocating work by behaviour is high-risk under the cited annex. This task adds no score and does not allocate shuttle work that way. The driver arranges the pickup. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited annex.

assumptions: The dispatcher writes the pickup card when the standing booking is set.
Fields are the customer or group, the place, the usual time, and the days.
The card does not name a driver's location or a mark.
If the row is missing, the driver reads the paper booking inside s1.
There is no native system to configure and no custom code.
Focal upkeep is zero because the dispatcher keeps the card, counted on the other line.
Works-council consultation for a location or behaviour system is out of scope because this design adds none.
unknowns: Whether this firm already keeps a standing pickup list in the cab.
research_questions: How often a regular group changes its usual time after the card is written.

incremental.description: No extra driver upkeep. The dispatcher keeps the pickup card.
The dispatcher writes the pickup card: customer or group, place, usual time, and days.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The standing days are often already known to this driver. The card saves the search only when the row is there and the group is not new.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Report a delay or accident by telephone or radio.

steps.what: Read which telephone or mobile radio this shuttle uses for a report.
Report delays, accidents, or other traffic and transportation situations using telephones or mobile radios on this shuttle.

tasks.design: A call card in the cab lists the depot telephone and the radio channel. The dispatcher writes it. The driver reads it, then speaks the delay, accident, or traffic situation on the telephone or the mobile radio. If the card has no row, the driver uses the written call list in the cab in the same step.
tasks.previous_blocker: The right number sat on a note at the depot, not next to the radio.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper card with the number and the channel is enough. No new model is required.
tasks.still_hard: What to say depends on the road in front of the driver. The other person has to hear it.
tasks.human_edge: The driver sees the delay and chooses what the depot needs to know first.
tasks.altitude: The driver still makes the report by telephone or radio. The card only shortens finding the number or the channel.

reach.task: Tell the depot about a delay
reach.learn: Read the call card, then still speak the delay on the radio.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the depot telephone and the radio channel shortens the search. The driver still speaks the report. Model knowledge.

Telematics and a driver app that observe location or behaviour need works-council consent under the cited article. This report stays a telephone or radio call and adds no telematics and no driver app. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited statute.

assumptions: The dispatcher writes the call card.
Fields are the depot telephone and the radio channel.
The card does not record the call.
If the row is missing, the driver reads the written call list in the cab inside s1.
The spoken report stays with the driver.
There is no native system to configure and no custom code.
Focal upkeep is zero because the dispatcher keeps the card.
A location or behaviour system is out of scope.
unknowns: Whether this shuttle already has the depot number fixed on the radio.
research_questions: How often the driver already knows the channel without looking.

incremental.description: No extra driver upkeep. The dispatcher keeps the call card.
The dispatcher writes the call card: depot telephone and radio channel.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of the task is the call itself. The card saves a short search, and only when the driver does not already know the number.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Complete an accident report after the scene.

steps.what: Read the vehicle card for this shuttle before the accident report.
Note at the scene what happened for this shuttle accident.
Complete accident reports when necessary, in this shuttle driver's own words.

tasks.design: A vehicle card in the cab lists the vehicle, the registration, and the insurer name. An office colleague writes it. The driver reads it, notes the scene, and writes the accident report when necessary. If the card has no row, the driver reads the paper vehicle folder in the cab inside the lookup. The report is the driver's own account on paper.
tasks.previous_blocker: Registration and insurer sat in an office file, so the driver hunted for them after the scene.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper card with those three fields is enough. No new model is required.
tasks.still_hard: What happened has to be written by the person who saw it. A card cannot supply that.
tasks.human_edge: The driver saw the accident and chooses what the report must say.
tasks.altitude: The driver still notes the scene and writes the report. The card only shortens finding the vehicle details.

reach.learn: The shuttle driver writes the account. The inspector still checks the scene facts.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the vehicle, registration, and insurer name shortens the search. The driver still writes the accident report. Model knowledge.

Telematics and a driver app that observe location or behaviour need works-council consent under the cited article. This report is paper and adds no telematics and no driver app. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited statute.

Scoring drivers or allocating work by behaviour is high-risk under the cited annex. This report adds no score and does not allocate work. The driver writes what happened. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited annex.

The cited fine concerned scanner indicators of exact idle time. This accident report records what the driver saw, not idle-time indicators. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited decision.

assumptions: An office colleague writes the vehicle card.
Fields are the vehicle, the registration, and the insurer name.
The card does not describe the accident and does not mark the driver.
If the row is missing, the driver reads the paper vehicle folder inside s1.
The scene note and the written report stay with the driver.
There is no native system to configure and no custom code.
Focal upkeep is zero because the office colleague keeps the card.
A location or behaviour system is out of scope.
unknowns: Which national accident form this firm must use, and whether a copy goes to an insurer.
research_questions: How often the registration is already printed on a label in the cab.

incremental.description: No extra driver upkeep. The office colleague keeps the vehicle card.
The office colleague writes the vehicle card: vehicle, registration, and insurer name.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The scene and the written account are almost all of the task. The card saves the vehicle lookup only when the accident happens and the row is already on the card.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the map and follow the directions.

steps.what: Read the maps note and the written geographic directions for this shuttle.
Follow the verbal directions while driving this shuttle.

tasks.design: A route card lists the stop, the street, and who gave the verbal note. The dispatcher writes it when the booking is set. The driver reads the maps note and the written geographic directions, then follows the verbal directions while driving. If the card has no row, the driver uses the paper map in the cab inside the lookup.
tasks.previous_blocker: The written turns were on the booking in the office, so the driver searched the map at the wheel.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper card with the stop, the street, and who spoke the note is enough. No new model is required.
tasks.still_hard: The road, a closure, and a passenger's verbal correction still have to be followed by the driver.
tasks.human_edge: The driver matches the note to the street in front of the shuttle.
tasks.altitude: The driver still reads the map and follows the directions. The card only shortens finding the written turns.

reach.learn: Read the route card, then still drive the turns.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the stop, the street, and who gave the verbal note shortens the search for the written directions. The driver still follows them. Model knowledge.

Telematics and a driver app that observe location or behaviour need works-council consent under the cited article. This task adds no telematics and no driver app. The driver reads the map. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited statute.

assumptions: The dispatcher writes the route card when the booking is set.
Fields are the stop, the street, and who gave the verbal note.
The card does not record where the shuttle is.
If the row is missing, the driver reads the paper map in the cab inside s1.
Following the directions stays with the driver.
There is no native system to configure and no custom code.
Focal upkeep is zero because the dispatcher keeps the card.
A location or behaviour system is out of scope.
unknowns: Whether regular shuttle runs already use a fixed stop list the driver knows by heart.
research_questions: How often a passenger's verbal correction overrides the written turns.

incremental.description: No extra driver upkeep. The dispatcher keeps the route card.
The dispatcher writes the route card: stop, street, and who gave the verbal note.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Driving and following the verbal directions are almost all of the task. The card saves the map search only on a run the driver does not already know.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The driver still arranges the pickup, reports the delay, writes the accident report, and follows the directions. A card only shortens finding the standing pickup, the call list, the vehicle details, or the written directions.
reach: A school bus driver can read a standing stop card and still agrees the pickup with the household.
A transit bus driver can read a call card and still speaks the delay.
A transportation inspector can read the driver's accident account and still checks the scene.
A light truck driver can read a route card and still drives the turns.
skills_to_grow: Open the paper booking, the call list, the vehicle folder, or the paper map when the card has no row.
Say what you saw on the radio, and write the accident account from the scene, not from the card.
role.ambitious_version: Cards do not arrange the pickup, make the radio report, write the accident account, or follow the road. The shuttle driver still does.
